claim: Development of the mammalian visual system proceeds in two stages: a first stage before birth in primates and before eye opening in altricial mammals where spontaneous activity shapes circuits in an activity-dependent but experience-independent manner, and a second stage where visual activity generated by sensory experience refines receptive fields.
source: Development of the mammalian visual system is thought to proceed in two stages. In the first stage, before birth in primates and before eye opening in altricial mammals, spontaneous activity generated by the retina and cortex shapes visual brain circuits in an activity-dependent but experience-independent manner. In the second stage, visual activity generated by sensory experience refines receptive fields.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature establishing this developmental framework.

claim: Many cells in ferrets with prematurely opened eyes exhibited low-pass temporal frequency tuning.
source: We observed that many cells in animals with prematurely opened eyes exhibited low-pass temporal frequency tuning and increased temporal frequency bandwidths, and these cells showed slightly increased orientation and direction selectivity index values.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from electrophysiological recordings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Spontaneous activity was greatly elevated in both hemispheres following the premature opening of one or both eyes in ferrets.
source: Spontaneous activity was greatly elevated in both hemispheres following the premature opening of one or both eyes, suggesting a global change in circuit excitability that was not restricted to cells that viewed the world through the prematurely opened eye.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from electrophysiological recordings.

claim: The elevation of spontaneous activity in both hemispheres suggests a global change in circuit excitability not restricted to cells that viewed the world through the prematurely opened eye.

claim: Premature visual experience alters circuit excitability and visual receptive fields, particularly with respect to temporal processing.
source: These results suggest that premature visual experience alters circuit excitability and visual receptive fields, in particular with respect to temporal processing.

claim: Closed lids in altricial mammals may serve to prevent visual experience until circuits are initially established and ready to be refined by visual experience.
source: We speculate that closed lids in altricial mammals serve to prevent visual experience until circuits are initially established and are ready to be refined by visual experience.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation based on the experimental findings.

claim: Molecular cues and spontaneous activity in retina and cortex guide initial circuit formation before the onset of visual experience.
source: Classically, these mechanisms have been divided into two sequential stages: an early stage, before the onset of visual experience, in which molecular cues and spontaneous activity in retina and cortex guide initial circuit formation (Katz and Shatz, 1996; Wong, 1999; Grubb et al., 2003; Cang et al., 2005; Smith et al., 2018), followed by a period in which activity driven by visual experience refines circuit function (Chapman et al., 1996; Huberman et al., 2008; Li et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2010; Chang et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Activity driven by visual experience refines circuit function after initial circuit formation.

evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: There is a rising population of human infants born very prematurely.

claim: Ferrets undergo a long postnatal developmental period.

claim: Ferrets are born with their eyes closed for 30-35 days.
source: Ferrets are born with their eyes closed – a condition that is maintained for 30–35 days (Issa et al., 1999) – making it possible to introduce inappropriately early visual experience by opening the lids with forceps, without introducing factors related to immature birth.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Issa et al., 1999.

claim: Eyes were opened early at postnatal day 25 in experimental ferrets, a developmental timepoint when retinal waves are still occurring.
source: Animals in both of the premature eye opening groups experienced early vision beginning on postnatal day 25, a developmental timepoint when retinal waves are still occurring (Meister et al., 1991; Wong et al., 1993), yet V1 is also responsive to visual input through the closed lids (Krug et al., 2001; Akerman et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Meister et al., 1991 and Wong et al., 1993.

claim: At postnatal day 25, V1 is responsive to visual input through the closed lids in ferrets.

claim: Visual input is capable of initiating retinal waves through the closed lids.
source: We hypothesized that this interaction may drive aberrant development of cortical receptive fields, as it is known that visual input is capable of initiating retinal waves through the closed lids (Tiriac et al., 2018).

claim: Animals with prematurely opened eyes received 8 hours total of visual exposure over 4 days.

claim: Electrophysiology experiments occurred between P55-68 in ferrets.

claim: By postnatal day 42, contrast sensitivity, orientation, direction, temporal frequency, and spatial frequency tuning have reached adult-like levels in ferrets.

source: Spontaneous firing rates were low in control animals (2.6 Hz) and were markedly increased in EO1ipsi hemispheres (11.1 Hz, p<1.09e-4), EO1contra hemispheres (6.6 Hz, p<0.0132), and EO2 hemispheres (6.6 Hz, p<0.0248).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis.

claim: Spontaneous firing rates were markedly increased in EO2 hemispheres (6.6 Hz, p<0.0248) compared to control.
source: Spontaneous firing rates were low in control animals (2.6 Hz) and were markedly increased in EO1ipsi hemispheres (11.1 Hz, p<1.09e-4), EO1contra hemispheres (6.6 Hz, p<0.0132), and EO2 hemispheres (6.6 Hz, p<0.0248).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis.

claim: Early eye opening induced long-term changes to circuit-level excitability that are not corrected during the remainder of development.
source: These results are consistent with the idea that early eye opening induces long-term changes to circuit-level excitability that are not corrected during the remainder of development.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings regarding spontaneous firing rates and suppression.

claim: The alterations in temporal frequency tuning identified in ferrets following premature eye opening are strongly suggestive of a deficit in motion processing.
source: The alterations in temporal frequency tuning identified in ferrets following premature eye opening are strongly suggestive of a deficit in motion processing.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the temporal frequency tuning results.

claim: The broadening of temporal frequency tuning curves and increase in the proportion of low-pass cells in V1 could translate to a decrease in the animal's ability to distinguish the temporal frequency (and perhaps the speed) of a moving visual stimulus.
source: The broadening of temporal frequency tuning curves and increase in the proportion of low-pass cells in V1 could translate to a decrease in the animal's ability to distinguish the temporal frequency (and perhaps the speed) of a moving visual stimulus.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Dark-reared cats and ferrets exhibit poor direction selectivity.
source: Dark-reared cats and ferrets exhibit poor direction selectivity (Imbert and Buisseret, 1975; Li et al., 2006), but dark-reared ferrets do not show strong deficits in temporal frequency processing.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Imbert and Buisseret, 1975 and Li et al., 2006.

claim: Dark-reared ferrets do not show strong deficits in temporal frequency processing.
source: Dark-reared cats and ferrets exhibit poor direction selectivity (Imbert and Buisseret, 1975; Li et al., 2006), but dark-reared ferrets do not show strong deficits in temporal frequency processing.
evidence: This is stated as a contrast to the findings in the current study.

claim: Cats raised in a strobe-light environment exhibited strong changes in subsequent direction selectivity.
source: Cats raised in a strobe-light environment (mostly after eye opening) exhibited strong changes in subsequent direction selectivity (Kennedy and Orban, 1983; Humphrey and Saul, 1998) and behavioral sensitivity to motion (Pasternak et al., 1981; Pasternak et al., 1985) that partially recovers with motion detection training.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kennedy and Orban, 1983 and Humphrey and Saul, 1998.

claim: Cats raised in a strobe-light environment exhibited changes in behavioral sensitivity to motion that partially recovers with motion detection training.
source: Cats raised in a strobe-light environment (mostly after eye opening) exhibited strong changes in subsequent direction selectivity (Kennedy and Orban, 1983; Humphrey and Saul, 1998) and behavioral sensitivity to motion (Pasternak et al., 1981; Pasternak et al., 1985) that partially recovers with motion detection training.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Pasternak et al., 1981 and Pasternak et al., 1985.

claim: Temporal frequency tuning is not subject to rapid modification shortly after eye opening in ferrets.
source: Temporal frequency tuning is not subject to rapid modification shortly after eye opening, as Ritter and colleagues demonstrated that providing ferrets that had just opened their eyes naturally with 6–9 hr of visual stimulation of a single temporal frequency did not elicit a shift in temporal frequency tuning (Ritter et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ritter et al., 2017.

claim: Providing ferrets that had just opened their eyes naturally with 6-9 hr of visual stimulation of a single temporal frequency did not elicit a shift in temporal frequency tuning.
source: Temporal frequency tuning is not subject to rapid modification shortly after eye opening, as Ritter and colleagues demonstrated that providing ferrets that had just opened their eyes naturally with 6–9 hr of visual stimulation of a single temporal frequency did not elicit a shift in temporal frequency tuning (Ritter et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ritter et al., 2017.

claim: Visual stimulation of a single temporal frequency causes a dramatic increase in direction selectivity in ferrets shortly after eye opening.
source: The same stimulation causes a dramatic increase in direction selectivity (Ritter et al., 2017) that normally develops in the first week to 10 days after eye opening and requires visual experience (Li et al., 2006; Li et al., 2008; Van Hooser et al., 2012; Roy et al., 2020b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ritter et al., 2017, Li et al., 2006, Li et al., 2008, Van Hooser et al., 2012, and Roy et al., 2020b.

claim: Mice that learned to hunt crickets in the critical period for ocular dominance plasticity exhibit lower low-pass index values.
source: The only manipulation we know of in the literature that has been shown to modify temporal frequency properties of developing animals is prey capture: mice that learned to hunt crickets in the critical period for ocular dominance plasticity exhibit lower low-pass index values (Bissen et al., 2025).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bissen et al., 2025.

claim: In the wild, mustelids raise their young in nests in the ground, in cavities such as holes in trees or caves, or in areas of dense vegetation.
source: In the wild, mustelids raise their young in nests in the ground, in cavities such as holes in trees or caves, or in areas of dense vegetation (Ruggiero et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ruggiero et al., 1994.

claim: Visual input before natural eye opening can drive activity in retina, LGN, and cortex in ferrets.
source: Although the light that reaches the close lids in developing ferrets is likely to be relatively dim, and any image-forming signal passing through the closed lids would be highly filtered in luminance, spatial frequency, and contrast, it is important to remember that visual input before natural eye opening (through the closed lids) can drive activity in retina, LGN, and cortex (Huttenlocher, 1967; Chapman and Stryker, 1993; Krug et al., 2001; Akerman et al., 2002; Akerman et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Huttenlocher, 1967, Chapman and Stryker, 1993, Krug et al., 2001, Akerman et al., 2002, and Akerman et al., 2004.

claim: Orientation selectivity can be observed through the closed lids in ferrets.
source: Further, orientation selectivity can be observed through the closed lids (Krug et al., 2001), indicating that some coarse image-forming information does make it through the closed lids.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Krug et al., 2001.

claim: Low-resolution visual input before natural eye opening plays a role in the development of ON-OFF segregation in dLGN.
source: The low-resolution visual input before natural eye opening is capable of driving activity in the visual circuit (Huttenlocher, 1967; Chapman and Stryker, 1993; Krug et al., 2001; Akerman et al., 2002; Akerman et al., 2004), and evidence shows that this early form of low-resolution visual experience plays a role in the development of ON-OFF segregation in dLGN (Akerman et al., 2002) and the initiation of retinal waves (Tiriac et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Akerman et al., 2002.

claim: GABAergic signaling has undergone its switch from providing primarily depolarizing input to hyperpolarizing input by P21-23 in ferrets.
source: GABAergic signaling has already undergone its switch (Ben-Ari, 2002) from providing primarily depolarizing input to hyperpolarizing input by P21-23 (Mulholland et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ben-Ari, 2002 and Mulholland et al., 2021.

claim: In the days prior to eye opening, inhibitory cells exhibit activity that is closely associated with the emerging functional modules that will reflect orientation columns.
source: In the days prior to eye opening, inhibitory cells exhibit activity that is closely associated with the emerging functional modules that will reflect orientation columns (Mulholland et al., 2021), but do not yet exhibit selectivity to orientation, in contrast to excitatory neurons, which do exhibit selectivity to orientation at that time (Chang and Fitzpatrick, 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mulholland et al., 2021.

claim: Inhibitory cells do not exhibit selectivity to orientation prior to eye opening, in contrast to excitatory neurons, which do exhibit selectivity to orientation at that time.
source: In the days prior to eye opening, inhibitory cells exhibit activity that is closely associated with the emerging functional modules that will reflect orientation columns (Mulholland et al., 2021), but do not yet exhibit selectivity to orientation, in contrast to excitatory neurons, which do exhibit selectivity to orientation at that time (Chang and Fitzpatrick, 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chang and Fitzpatrick, 2022.

claim: Homeostatic mechanisms such as synaptic scaling and regulation of intrinsic excitability operate during the critical period for ocular dominance plasticity.
source: Homeostatic mechanisms such as synaptic scaling (Desai et al., 1999, Turrigiano et al., 1998), and regulation of intrinsic excitability (Desai et al., 1999; Hengen et al., 2013) operate during the critical period for ocular dominance plasticity and serve to keep ongoing firing rates within a cell-defined range (Hengen et al., 2013; Hengen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Desai et al., 1999, Turrigiano et al., 1998, Hengen et al., 2013, and Hengen et al., 2016.

claim: Homeostatic mechanisms serve to keep ongoing firing rates within a cell-defined range.
source: Homeostatic mechanisms such as synaptic scaling (Desai et al., 1999, Turrigiano et al., 1998), and regulation of intrinsic excitability (Desai et al., 1999; Hengen et al., 2013) operate during the critical period for ocular dominance plasticity and serve to keep ongoing firing rates within a cell-defined range (Hengen et al., 2013; Hengen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hengen et al., 2013 and Hengen et al., 2016.

claim: Bilateral enucleation of ferrets induces anomalies in the distribution of callosal cells in primary visual cortex.
source: Work in ferrets and rats suggests a role for retinal waves in the development of interhemispheric connectivity; bilateral enucleation of ferrets induces anomalies in the distribution of callosal cells in primary visual cortex (Bock et al., 2012), and results in callosal projections connecting topographically mismatched loci in VC in P4-6 rats (Olavarria and Hiroi, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bock et al., 2012.

claim: Bilateral enucleation results in callosal projections connecting topographically mismatched loci in visual cortex in P4-6 rats.
source: Work in ferrets and rats suggests a role for retinal waves in the development of interhemispheric connectivity; bilateral enucleation of ferrets induces anomalies in the distribution of callosal cells in primary visual cortex (Bock et al., 2012), and results in callosal projections connecting topographically mismatched loci in VC in P4-6 rats (Olavarria and Hiroi, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Olavarria and Hiroi, 2003.

claim: Retinal waves demonstrate coordinated activity between both hemispheres in mice and ferrets.
source: Further, retinal waves demonstrate coordinated activity between both hemispheres in mice and ferrets (Weliky and Katz, 1999; Ackman et al., 2012; Ackman and Crair, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Weliky and Katz, 1999, Ackman et al., 2012, and Ackman and Crair, 2014.

claim: There is a transient retina to retina connection in mice and ferret, which exists during the period of retinal waves.
source: Recent findings describe a transient retina to retina connection in mice and ferret, which exists during the period of retinal waves (Murcia-Belmonte et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Murcia-Belmonte et al., 2019.

claim: Lichliter and colleagues prematurely opened the shells of bobwhite quail eggs and provided visual experience to the chick and found a subsequent loss of visual selectivity to bobwhite hens vs. hens of another species.
source: Lichliter and colleagues (Lickliter, 2018; Lickliter, 2000; Sleigh and Casey, 2014) prematurely opened the shells of bobwhite quail eggs and provided visual experience to the chick and found a subsequent loss of visual selectivity to bobwhite hens vs. hens of another species (Sleigh and Lickliter, 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lickliter, 2018, Lickliter, 2000, Sleigh and Casey, 2014, and Sleigh and Lickliter, 1995.

claim: Premature visual experience in bobwhite quail caused multi-modal impacts on auditory processing, in that animals failed to eventually become responsive to cross-species hen calls.
source: Further, they demonstrated multi-modal impacts on auditory processing after premature visual experience, in that animals failed to eventually become responsive to cross-species hen calls.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the Lichliter studies.

claim: In behavioral studies of rats whose eyes were prematurely opened 7 days early, opening a single eye (but not opening both eyes early) caused a deficit in pivoting locomotor reactions on the side of the early-opened eye.
source: In behavioral studies of rats whose eyes were prematurely opened 7 days early, investigators found that opening a single eye (but not opening both eyes early) caused a deficit in pivoting locomotor reactions on the side of the early-opened eye; that is, rats pivoted more frequently towards stimuli viewed through the eye that opened on time (Foreman and Altaha, 1991).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Foreman and Altaha, 1991.

claim: Very premature human babies exhibit a variety of visual deficits later in life that are not explained by the condition of the eye, broadly termed Cortical/Cerebral Visual Impairment (CVI).
source: Very premature human babies exhibit a variety of visual deficits later in life that are not explained by the condition of the eye, broadly termed Cortical/Cerebral Visual Impairment (CVI; Ortibus et al., 2009; Kozeis, 2010; Dutton, 2013; Sakki et al., 2018; Pamir et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ortibus et al., 2009, Kozeis, 2010, Dutton, 2013, Sakki et al., 2018, and Pamir et al., 2021.

claim: Studies that have excluded individuals with known brain damage or retinal problems have found that extreme prematurity itself has an impact on later vision, particularly on motion perception.
source: But studies that have excluded individuals with known brain damage or retinal problems (or analyzed these populations separately) have also found that extreme prematurity itself has an impact on later vision, particularly on motion perception (Atkinson and Braddick, 2007; Benassi et al., 2018; Guzzetta et al., 2009; Hou et al., 2011; MacKay et al., 2005) and sometimes lowered visual acuity (Jain et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Atkinson and Braddick, 2007, Benassi et al., 2018, Guzzetta et al., 2009, Hou et al., 2011, MacKay et al., 2005, and Jain et al., 2022.

claim: Extreme prematurity sometimes results in lowered visual acuity.
source: But studies that have excluded individuals with known brain damage or retinal problems (or analyzed these populations separately) have also found that extreme prematurity itself has an impact on later vision, particularly on motion perception (Atkinson and Braddick, 2007; Benassi et al., 2018; Guzzetta et al., 2009; Hou et al., 2011; MacKay et al., 2005) and sometimes lowered visual acuity (Jain et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jain et al., 2022.

claim: The data are consistent with the idea that inappropriately early visual stimulation contributes to deficits in motion processing in very premature human babies.
source: Our data are consistent with the idea that inappropriately early visual stimulation contributes to deficits in motion processing.
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting the ferret experimental findings to human premature birth outcomes.

claim: Premature patterned vision has a long-lasting impact on the development of receptive fields in the visual cortex.
source: Regardless of whether premature patterned vision has a clinically relevant role for human vision, the experiments here demonstrate clearly that premature patterned vision has a long-lasting impact on the development of receptive fields in the visual cortex.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings.

claim: The evolved late eye opening of many rodents and carnivores, and the prolonged prenatal period of primates, may help to protect the visual system from exposure to high luminance, high contrast, and high spatial frequency stimulation until the visual system is ready for this type of stimulation.
source: The results suggest that the evolved late eye opening of many rodents and carnivores, and the prolonged prenatal period of primates, may help to protect the visual system from exposure to high luminance, high contrast, and high spatial frequency stimulation until the visual system is ready for this type of stimulation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental findings in an evolutionary context.

claim: A total of 27 female ferrets were used in the study.
source: For the entire study, a total of 27 female ferrets were used and all experimental procedures were carried out between postnatal days P55–68.
evidence: This describes the experimental subjects used in the study.

claim: 17 animals had one eye prematurely opened.
source: We studied 17 animals that had one eye prematurely opened, 4 animals that had both eyes opened, and 11 controls.
evidence: This describes the experimental groups in the study.

claim: 4 animals had both eyes prematurely opened.
source: We studied 17 animals that had one eye prematurely opened, 4 animals that had both eyes opened, and 11 controls.
evidence: This describes the experimental groups in the study.

claim: 11 control animals were studied.
source: We studied 17 animals that had one eye prematurely opened, 4 animals that had both eyes opened, and 11 controls.
evidence: This describes the experimental groups in the study.

claim: Recordings were made in monocular visual cortex.
source: In this study, all recordings were performed in the monocular visual cortex in order to simplify the interpretation of these changes without needing to consider interactions between the two eyes.
evidence: This describes the recording location in the experimental protocol.

claim: EO1contra cells exhibited significantly lower L50 values than control animals (p<0.002).
source: E01contra cells exhibited significantly lower L50 values than control animals (p<0.002, LMEM).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: EO2 cells exhibited widened temporal frequency bandwidths by showing increased H50 values (p<0.004).
source: EO2 cells, by contrast, exhibited widened bandwidths by showing increased H50 values (p<0.004, LMEM).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: EO1contra cells exhibited significantly lower absolute L50 values compared to control cells (p<0.00029).
source: Considering the absolute value of the temporal frequency response (where deviations above or below background firing rates contributed to response), EO1contra cells again exhibited significantly lower L50 values compared to control cells (p<0.00029, LMEM).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: EO1ipsi cells exhibited a slight increase in absolute L50 values (p<0.0148).
source: EO1ipsi cells exhibited a slight increase in L50 values (p<0.0148, LMEM).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: EO1ipsi cells showed a substantial increase in absolute H50 cutoff values (p<0.00169).
source: EO1ipsi cells showed a substantial increase in absolute H50 cutoff values (p<0.00169, LMEM).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.
